Let  

\[
N=\lfloor r\rfloor,\qquad 
S_r=\sum_{i=1}^{N}\sqrt{r^2-i^2}.
\]

The given formula is

\[
f(r)=1+4N+4\sum_{i=1}^{N}\left\lfloor \sqrt{r^2-i^2}\right\rfloor .
\]

For any \(t\ge 0\),

\[
t-1\le \lfloor t\rfloor \le t.
\]

Thus

\[
f(r)\ge 1+4N+4\sum_{i=1}^{N}\left(\sqrt{r^2-i^2}-1\right)
=1+4S_r,
\]

and

\[
f(r)\le 1+4N+4S_r.
\]

Now consider the decreasing function

\[
g(x)=\sqrt{r^2-x^2},\qquad 0\le x\le r.
\]

Because \(g\) is decreasing,

\[
S_r=\sum_{i=1}^{N} g(i)\le \int_0^N g(x)\,dx
\le \int_0^r g(x)\,dx.
\]

But

\[
\int_0^r \sqrt{r^2-x^2}\,dx
=\frac{\pi r^2}{4},
\]

the area of a quarter circle of radius \(r\). Therefore

\[
4S_r\le \pi r^2.
\]

So

\[
f(r)\le 1+4N+4S_r
\le 1+4r+\pi r^2.
\]

For the lower bound, since \(g\) is decreasing,

\[
S_r\ge \int_1^r g(x)\,dx
= \int_0^r g(x)\,dx-\int_0^1 g(x)\,dx.
\]

Since \(\sqrt{r^2-x^2}\le r\) on \([0,1]\),

\[
\int_0^1 \sqrt{r^2-x^2}\,dx\le r.
\]

Hence

\[
S_r\ge \frac{\pi r^2}{4}-r,
\]

and therefore

\[
4S_r\ge \pi r^2-4r.
\]

Thus

\[
f(r)\ge 1+4S_r
\ge 1+\pi r^2-4r.
\]

Combining the bounds,

\[
\pi r^2-4r+1
\le f(r)
\le \pi r^2+4r+1.
\]

Dividing by \(\pi r^2\),

\[
1-\frac{4r-1}{\pi r^2}
\le \frac{f(r)}{\pi r^2}
\le
1+\frac{4r+1}{\pi r^2}.
\]

As \(r\to\infty\), both the lower and upper bounds tend to \(1\). By the squeeze theorem,

\[
\lim_{r\to\infty}\frac{f(r)}{\pi r^2}=1.
\]

\[
\boxed{1}
\]

27B·v4.method: Floor bounds reduce to bounding the sum S; monotone-function integral comparison gives S = πr²/4 + O(r); squeeze yields limit 1.
